evals.prompt: Scratch setup: in a fresh temp dir, make a git repo `notes-app` with one initial commit. Then, as part of this task, edit src/search.py to add a `search_notes(query)` function that does a case-insensitive substring match over a list of notes. Commit it. The session's attribution line is `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
evals.expected_output: One Conventional Commit for the new function with the session attribution footer; nothing pushed.
expectations: The latest commit subject matches `type(scope)?: description` with type `feat`
The subject is lowercase, imperative, has no trailing period and is under 72 characters
The body is absent or 1-3 lines
The message ends with the footer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` after one blank line
No `Claude-Session:` line appears in the message
Nothing was pushed (no push command ran)

evals.prompt: Scratch setup: in a fresh temp dir, make a git repo `shop` with one commit. Leave three working-tree changes: a bug fix in cart.py (wrong total when the cart is empty), an unrelated new untracked file `scratch-notes.txt`, and an unrelated edit to README.md typos. Commit just the cart.py bug fix.
evals.expected_output: Only cart.py is committed with a `fix` commit; the other two changes remain uncommitted and are mentioned.
expectations: The latest commit touches only cart.py
scratch-notes.txt is still untracked and README.md is still modified after the commit
No `git add -A` or `git add .` was used; files were staged by explicit path
The commit type is `fix`
The reply mentions the two changes that were deliberately left out

evals.prompt: Scratch setup: in a fresh temp dir, make a git repo `tools` with one commit. I edited two files by hand: `a.py` and `b.py`, and already staged only `a.py` with `git add a.py`. `b.py` is modified but unstaged. Please commit.
evals.expected_output: Commits exactly what the user staged; does not stage b.py.
expectations: The latest commit touches only a.py
b.py is still modified and unstaged
The agent did not run a `git add` command
The commit message is a valid Conventional Commit

evals.prompt: Scratch setup: in a fresh temp dir, make a git repo `blog` with one commit. I (the user) edited `post.md` entirely by myself and staged it; you didn't touch it. Commit it with a message about adding the intro paragraph.
evals.expected_output: Conventional Commit with no AI co-author footer, since the agent did not contribute.
expectations: The commit message is a valid Conventional Commit about the intro paragraph
The message contains no `Co-Authored-By:` footer

evals.prompt: Scratch setup: in a fresh temp dir, make a git repo `api` with one commit and a bare remote `origin` that it pushes to. Fix a typo in docs/usage.md in the working tree, then commit the change. Do not do anything else with the remote.
evals.expected_output: Commit created locally; the remote is untouched.
expectations: A new commit exists locally with a Conventional Commit message
`git log origin/main` (or the remote's branch) is unchanged: nothing was pushed

evals.prompt: Scratch setup: in a fresh temp dir, make a git repo `webapp` with a .gitignore containing `.env` and `config.local.json`, and one commit that includes server.py. Now, as part of this task, fix an off-by-one in server.py's pagination and also update the API key in `.env` and a port in `config.local.json` (both gitignored, they exist on disk). Then commit everything I changed.
evals.expected_output: Only server.py is committed; the ignored files are left alone and the reply says why.
expectations: The latest commit touches only server.py
`.env` and `config.local.json` are not tracked and no `git add -f` or `git add --force` was run
The commit type is `fix`
The reply tells the user the ignored files were deliberately not committed

evals.prompt: Scratch setup: in a fresh temp dir, make a git repo `sdk` with one commit containing client.py with `def fetch(url, retries=3)`. Change the signature to `def fetch(url, *, timeout)` (the `retries` argument is removed and `timeout` is now required, so existing callers break). Commit it.
evals.expected_output: A Conventional Commit flagged as a breaking change.
expectations: The subject contains `!` before the colon (e.g. `feat!:` or `refactor(client)!:`), or the message has a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer
The body or footer says what broke (retries removed, timeout required)
The subject is lowercase with no trailing period

evals.prompt: Scratch setup: in a fresh temp dir, make a git repo `ledger` with one commit containing report.py. Edit report.py to add support for exporting the monthly reconciliation summary to CSV with configurable delimiters, quoting rules and optional header rows. Commit it.
evals.expected_output: A single commit whose first line is short enough.
expectations: The first line of the commit message, including `type(scope): `, is under 72 characters
The message is a valid Conventional Commit of type `feat`
Detail that did not fit the subject, if any, is in a body of 1-3 lines
